_doc: ⚑ S190 — THE SEARCH, 1997 (Phase 5; his idea, 2026-09-28: 'the idea should be inside of the computer interactions, as it gives a directly and important claim that there was already an infrastructure behind this digital point… a browser… based on the shame felt'; 'from early internet explorer to modern Chrome'). After the kit's dial-up the browser opens, the search field already holding tonight's query and the history below it holding the nights before (no free typing — the law). The results are the network: a links directory by state, a testimony page, a college page with international referrals and an anonymous mailer, a webring, the channel. Every page carries the ring's bar and the channel's Join; the search is how he finds the channel. The third page of results never loads. GROUNDING (docs/reinterp/SOURCES_1997_WEB_2026-09-27.md; his research SocialMedia_Deep.md §1): directories by state and by country from 1996; webrings; counters; an anonymous mailer (1996); 'search engine / Christian website → testimony → links page → ministry → forum/chat' as the documented path, the specific search [I]. 1997 engines did not autocomplete, so the history carries the earlier queries. Every mark here is INVENTED (NetPilot, Seekr, Fellowship Links, the Walking-Out Ring, the pages' addresses).

_docS194: ⚑ S194 — his notes (2026-09-28, PLAN_WEB_AND_HELPERS §1–2): 'will the user understand the connection of it IRC here?… maybe it instructs to open the browser, and when you open it it already has the content'; 'the ministry website with resources being links to pages of opinion of these SOGICE therapists'; 'do what is missing — the ring list'. So the dial-up lands on the fellowship's PORTAL (the kit's home page) — it names the channel and has one big Join, the search under it, and Resources; the ring's List shows its member sites (two 'under construction', period-true — his archive's yellow squares). Every Resources page speaks a DOCUMENTED position of the period in the seller's voice and carries its dossier mark (the practice it is a trace of): 'Understanding the Root' → the questionnaire's self-therapy theory (origin_intake_e1#0); 'A Letter to Parents' → the conference guide's warning signs and enlisting of relatives, coaches and pastors (#1); 'Summer Youth Weekend' → the placement (#3). The counsellor is invented; no real person, likeness or quotation.

_docS198: ⚑ S198 — his visual archive (2026-09-29): 1998's discovery was a DIRECTORY as much as a search — Yahoo's hand-curated category tree, its category matches listed ABOVE the site matches on a results page (documented, the 30 June 1998 capture). So Seekr has a directory: the path down to 'Ex-Gay', its sub-categories with counts ('@' marks a category cross-listed from elsewhere in the tree, as Yahoo did), and its site listings — the ring's members. The results page names the category first. Every mark invented.
